note_on_method: Every court count and address below is quoted from that venue's own facility page on stpaul.gov, in the City's amenity format. The City publishes no list of its pickleball venues, so the candidate names came from its own pickleball GIS layer and each one was then checked against a page. Where a page says nothing about lighting, cost, hours or surface, these notes say so. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description:
One pickleball court, and the City is unusually direct about what kind: its amenity list reads "1 Pickleball court (striped tennis court)". That parenthesis is the whole venue in five words: a tennis court with pickleball lines on it, on the East Side of Saint Paul at Arlington and Arkwright. It is the smallest published venue in the city, and among the smallest anywhere in this directory.

There is one playing surface and it is primarily a tennis court. If anyone is using it for tennis there is no pickleball here at all. That is different from a two-court venue where you might wait, and very different from Edgcumbe's four courts across town.
slots.getting_there: 400 Arlington Ave. E., Saint Paul, MN 55130, which the Census geocoder matched to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. This is the East Side, north of Phalen. The City publishes no parking guidance, and on a neighbourhood park the realistic expectation is the street.
slots.what_to_expect: One court, shared with tennis, and almost nothing else on the record. Saint Paul's facility pages are amenity inventories: they list what is at a site and say nothing about opening hours, cost, lighting or surface. So there is one striped court at this address, and the City states nothing about when it is open, what it costs, whether it is lit or what it is made of.

faqs.a: One, striped onto a tennis court. The City's amenity list reads "1 Pickleball court (striped tennis court)", the only venue in Saint Paul where it spells out the overlay in the count line itself.
Not stated. No Saint Paul facility page states lighting for a pickleball court either way, so all six published venues read "not stated" on the point.

faqs.q: What if someone is playing tennis?
faqs.a: Then there is no pickleball here. With one court and no dedicated surface, tennis and pickleball cannot both happen.

faqs.q: Where else can I play nearby?
faqs.a: Duluth and Case Recreation Center has two courts on the East Side. Across the city, Edgcumbe Recreation Center's four are the largest published count in Saint Paul.

faqs.q: Is this really the smallest venue in the city?
faqs.a: Of the six published, yes: one court against two at four venues and four at Edgcumbe. It is also among the smallest venues anywhere in this directory, alongside single-court sites in Madison, Austin and Saint Paul's own park system.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts striped onto the park's two tennis courts, in the Hamline-Midway area adjacent to Newell Park. Clayland is the one Saint Paul venue where the City writes a sentence about the place rather than only listing what is in it: the park "features two tennis courts striped for pickleball as well as two designated handball courts". Designated handball courts are rare in a municipal park inventory, and they tell you this is a site built for racquet and ball sports generally rather than for pickleball in particular.

Two courts is the typical Saint Paul venue; four of the six published here have exactly two. What is not typical is that Clayland appears nowhere on the City's own pickleball map, despite its facility page carrying a count. Edgcumbe Recreation Center is in the same position. A player using the City's map would not find this park, and a player using its facility pages would.
slots.getting_there: 901 Fairview Ave. N., Saint Paul, MN 55104, matched by the Census geocoder to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. Fairview Avenue runs north-south through Hamline-Midway, and the park sits beside Newell Park. No parking guidance is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts on two tennis courts, so the competing use is tennis and the surface is a tennis surface, which the City does not name. Nothing is published about hours, lighting or cost. Alongside the tennis and pickleball there are two designated handball courts, which means a busy afternoon here is a busy afternoon for several sports at once.

faqs.a: Two, from the amenity list: "(2) Pickleball Courts". The City's park description says the same thing in words: "two tennis courts striped for pickleball".

faqs.q: Is this park on the City's pickleball map?
faqs.a: No. Clayland states a pickleball count on its own facility page and appears nowhere in the City's pickleball GIS layer. Edgcumbe Recreation Center is in the same position. This page publishes from the facility pages, because the pages are what state a number.

faqs.q: What else is at the park?
faqs.a: Two tennis courts (the same courts, striped) and two designated handball courts, per the City's description. The park is adjacent to Newell Park.
Not stated. Saint Paul publishes no cost for any of its pickleball venues. They are municipal park courts and are very likely free, but "very likely" is not a fact.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts at an East Side recreation centre, and outside it. The City splits this facility's amenities into Indoor and Outdoor, and the pickleball line sits under "Outdoor Amenities:", alongside a football field, a flag football field, a soccer field, a playground, a picnic area, two baseball fields and three Kato/Sepak Takraw courts. The building itself holds a small gym, a small kitchen and a multipurpose room, and the City publishes no pickleball count for any of them.

Kato, or Sepak Takraw, is a kick-volleyball game played widely in the Hmong community, and Saint Paul is one of very few American cities whose parks department builds courts for it. A recreation centre with staff, a building and several fields is a different proposition from a bare neighbourhood park, even when the court count is identical.
slots.getting_there: 1020 Duluth St., Saint Paul, MN 55106, matched by the Census geocoder to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. This is the East Side, and Arlington/Arkwright Park's single court is the nearest other published venue. No parking information is published, though a staffed recreation centre with several sports fields will have some.
slots.what_to_expect: Two outdoor courts on the grounds of a recreation centre, which is a slightly better prospect than a bare park: there is a building, staff and other facilities on site. What the City does not publish is when any of it is open to pickleball, what it costs, or whether the courts are lit. That silence covers all six Saint Paul venues on this site.

faqs.a: No. The City lists them under "Outdoor Amenities:" rather than "Indoor Amenities:". The centre's indoor space is a small gym, a kitchen and a multipurpose room, with no pickleball count published for any of it.
Two: "(2) Pickleball Courts" in the outdoor amenity list.

faqs.q: What else is on the site?
faqs.a: A football field, a flag football field, a soccer field, two baseball fields, a playground, a picnic area, a bike rack, a garden for children and three Kato/Sepak Takraw courts.

faqs.q: Is the recreation centre open when the courts are?
faqs.a: Not published. The City states no hours for the building or the courts on this page. The courts are outdoors, so building hours and court access are not necessarily the same question.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, the largest published count in Saint Paul and double what a typical venue here offers. They are outdoor, listed under "Outdoor Amenities:", beside a baseball field and a hockey rink, at a staffed recreation centre in the Macalester-Groveland area. The indoor space runs to a medium gym, a fitness centre, a craft room, a game room, a preschool room, two racquetball/walleyball courts and a warming room.

Four courts is not many by the standards of the larger cities on this site: Austin has an eight-court venue, Scottsdale a ten, but in Saint Paul it is double the median and the only place where capacity is not the binding constraint. Like Clayland Park, it is absent from the City's own pickleball map despite carrying a count on its page.
slots.getting_there: 320 Griggs St. S., Saint Paul, MN 55105, matched by the Census geocoder to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. Macalester-Groveland, in the south-west of the city. No parking guidance is published, though the site has a staffed building, a ball field and a hockey rink and is not a pocket park.
slots.what_to_expect: The best odds in Saint Paul of getting on a court. Four outdoor courts, a building with facilities beside them, and, as at every Saint Paul venue, no published hours, no published cost, no lighting statement and no named surface. The warming room in the indoor list is a reminder of the climate: nothing on the City's pages says what happens to these courts between November and March.

faqs.a: Four: "(4) Pickleball Courts", the largest published count in Saint Paul. The next largest venues have two.
No. They sit under the centre's "Outdoor Amenities:" heading. The indoor space includes a medium gym and two racquetball/walleyball courts, and the City publishes no pickleball count for either.

faqs.q: Can I play here in winter?
faqs.a: Nothing is published either way. These are outdoor courts in Minnesota and the centre has a warming room for its hockey rink, which tells you about the season without telling you about the courts.

faqs.q: How does this compare with the rest of the city?
faqs.a: It is the largest published venue in Saint Paul by a factor of two. Clayland, Duluth and Case, Homecroft and Orchard each have two courts, and Arlington/Arkwright has one: thirteen courts across six sites in total.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts in the Highland area of south-west Saint Paul, listed in the City's amenity inventory alongside two tennis courts and a tennis backboard. That is as clear a picture of the arrangement as an inventory can give without a sentence: the pickleball is on the tennis courts, and there is a backboard for practising against when nobody else is about.

Homecroft has a short amenity list with nothing much competing for the space: open space, the courts, the backboard. Edgcumbe Recreation Center is a short distance away, which makes this quarter the best-served part of published Saint Paul: six of the city's thirteen courts are in those two venues. Choosing between them comes down to the count.
slots.getting_there: 1850 Sheridan Ave., Saint Paul, MN 55116, matched by the Census geocoder to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. Highland, in the south-west of the city, not far from Edgcumbe Recreation Center's four courts, which is the obvious alternative when two are not enough. The City publishes no parking guidance.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts striped on tennis courts, a tennis backboard, and open space. Nothing is published about hours, cost, lighting or surface, which is true of every Saint Paul venue on this site. The realistic read: a quiet neighbourhood venue for a pair or two, with the city's largest venue a short distance away for anything bigger.

faqs.a: Two: "(2) Pickleball Courts" in the City's amenity list, alongside "(2) Tennis Courts".

Almost certainly. The City lists two tennis courts and two pickleball courts at a park whose pickleball page rule says outdoor pickleball courts are located on tennis courts. It does not spell out the overlay for this venue specifically, as it does at Arlington/Arkwright and Clayland.
Not stated. No Saint Paul facility page states lighting for a pickleball court.
A solid wall for practising strokes against alone. The City lists one here alongside the two tennis courts and two pickleball courts.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts and, listed separately in the same amenity inventory, "1 Tennis Court (w/ pickleball lines)". Orchard Park is the only venue in Saint Paul where the City's own list implies more playable pickleball than the number it gives, and this page publishes the smaller, stated figure: two. The lined tennis court is a third surface you may well be able to use if it is free, and it is not added to the count because the City counts it as a tennis court.

A count of three would mean deciding how the City categorises its own courts; ignoring the third entirely would hide something a player would want. So the number is two and the sentence is here.
slots.getting_there: 875 Orchard Ave., Saint Paul, MN 55103, matched by the Census geocoder to St. Paul city, Ramsey County. This is the North End. The City publishes no parking guidance for this or any other Saint Paul pickleball venue.
slots.what_to_expect: Two counted courts plus a lined tennis court, all outdoor, with nothing published about hours, cost, lighting or surface. If the two pickleball courts are busy it is worth looking at the tennis court. The City has put pickleball lines on it, which is as close to an invitation as an amenity list gets.

faqs.a: Two, as the City counts them: "2 Pickleball Courts". Its list separately shows "1 Tennis Court (w/ pickleball lines)", which is described here but not added to the count, because the City counts it as a tennis court.

faqs.q: So can I play on three courts or two?
faqs.a: Two are pickleball courts. The third is a tennis court with pickleball lines on it, which you may be able to use when it is free.
Not stated. No Saint Paul venue on this site has a lighting statement either way.

faqs.q: Is the North End well served for pickleball?
faqs.a: On the published record, thinly: Orchard's two courts are the only pickleball in that part of the city. The City's map shows further sites nearby, including Rice Recreation Center, whose facility page states no court count.
